It is distinct for its complex 'Elected Suit' ranking, legal partnership communication, and the use of the 'KarnÃ¶ffel' (Unter) as the master card. It is one of the oldest game formats still played in Europe.

Derived directly from the 15th-century KarnÃ¶ffel, it preserved the unique medieval ranking systems that most other card games lost. KnÃ¼ffeln specifically became associated with the farming communities of Oldenburg.
48 cards. Use two sets of 24 cards or remove Aces from 52. Standard ranks 2-10, Jack, Queen, King.

Each player receives 9 cards (dealt 3-3-3). One card is turned up to determine the elected suit.

items.text: Jann: When a team wins the first five tricks in a row they score double (Jann).
Durchmarsch (March): If a team wins all nine tricks they achieve a march; in many rules this scores triple or quadruple, and players may receive a punch or the slate ladder is redrawn.

Raising the stakes (Drein un Seen): A team that has won two tricks may lead a card face down to double the points; opponents may look and accept or concede. In later rules this may be played at any time.
